question: If two circles of radii 35 cm and 25 cm touch each other externally, then the length (in cm) of a common tangent is (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the first circle (R₁) = 35 cm

Radius of the second circle (R₂) = 25 cm

**Formula Used:**

Length of the common external tangent = √{d² - (R1 - R2)²}

**Calculation:**

Distance between the centers of the circles (d) = R₁ + R₂

d = 35 + 25

d = 60 cm

Length of the common external tangent = √{d² - (R1 - R2)²}

√{60² - (35 - 25)²}

√{60² - 10²}

√{3600 - 100}

√3500 ≈ 59.16

Length of the common external tangent = 59.16 cm

**The length of the common tangent is 59.16 cm.**
